Coastal Cleanups Coastal Cleanups 
Each year, the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement partners 
with Be the Solution to Pollution to support coastal cleanups 
throughout the SouthCoast region. Founded by Mary 
Lou Nicholson, recipient of the Leduc Center for Civic 
Engagement’s 2024 Community Member Civic Leadership 
Award, Be the Solution to Pollution’s mission is to raise 
awareness about the dangers of plastic pollution. In addition 
to organizing regular shoreline cleanups, they promote 
alternatives to single-use plastics, deliver educational 
presentations in schools, screen documentaries on plastic 
waste, and host informational tables at local events. 
This year, 43 UMass Dartmouth students took part in seven 
shoreline cleanups across the SouthCoast region. Cleanup 
efforts spanned several locations, including Fort Phoenix, 
Hedge Street, and Marsh Island in Fairhaven; Riverside Park 
Shoreline, East Beach, and West Beach in New Bedford; and 
Jones Beach in Dartmouth. Together, the students removed a 
total of 1,636 lbs. of litter from these coastal areas, including 
406 cigarettes and 754 pieces of single-use plastic items such 
as bottles, caps, and shopping bags. 
By removing 1,636 pounds of litter, predominantly single- 
use plastics, UMass Dartmouth students not only improved 
our local shorelines but also contributed to the global fight 
against plastic pollution.
